text_fidelity_a:
Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray) For my daughter's sake, I would give this camera 5 stars. It is the longest lasting favorite toy any of my kids have ever received, EVER. I bought it for my then 7 year old daughter for Christmas 2 years ago, and it is still her very favorite toy at age 9. She plays with it almost daily, takes it with her on trips and to important events, and shows everyone the pictures she takes. I think not much more praise can be had for a toy than for it to be beloved after two full years of daily play! But I wills say, her expectations for it are different than mine. She doesn't care about printing the pictures out. She likes taking them and looking at them on the viewfinder, projecting them on the wall, and using the added features to make funny frames around the people and funny sounds. That's all she wants from it, and it delivers that perfectly.

BUT, as a parent, I would have hoped the screen would be better quality. When you look at it, it's sort of blurry and got lines through it. Frankly, sometimes it's hard to tell what I'm looking at. This doesn't bother my now 9 year old daughter AT ALL. But it is disappointing to me because I know the technology exists to make that better.

The quality of pictures is also not great when uploaded onto my computer (which I've only done a couple of times). It's VERY pixelated. Again, this isn't a feature my daughter cares about, so take that into account, but for me I wish that the option were there to print out a decent quality print because sometimes she takes really awesome shots that I wish I could save.

This camera is also super tough. Despite being dropped and thrown around and fought over by siblings for the last 2 years, it still works perfectly. The batteries last her generally a few months, depending on play. But they're just AA's, so no biggie to change them out.

Really, I am most impressed that this toy continues to make her so happy. I think Playskool could go a long way to making the picture/screen quality better, even for kids, but that's just a mom talking!
text_fidelity_b: Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray)

WireJewelry Double Barrel Rock Tumbler with (2) 3 Pound Capacity Drums My boys young boys have been rockhounds ever since we moved to Eastern Oregon three years ago. We thought we'd add the the thrill and enjoyment by getting them a tumbler to further explore the joys of rock hunting. There's a certain thrill of putting in raw stones that you think are "pretty", only to see their true beauty one they are polished.

We already have a single barrel WireJewelry tumbler and love it so much that we decided to grab this one to expand our capability. (There are LOTS of rocks here).

As before, assembly and setup was easy. Allowing one to have six total pounds of capacity is amazing. The heavy duty motor doesn't seem to be strained at all, even under full load, so it should last years. The barrel construction is very sturdy and we have never had even a minor leak. By design, they are very well sealed. While the noise level is not bad, I find it best to do my rock tumbling in the garage. The same hum in your house for weeks on end might just get to you.

This company is great for packaging kits, not only for the tumbling media, but for rocks as well. The media kids come numbered and labeled, so the process is super easy to follow. Tumbling is not a quick hobby... each batch can take weeks. Personally, I think that's part of the fun.

If you are thinking of getting into the hobby, I definitely recommend products from WireJewelry, I have yet to be disappointed in their products. Enjoy the treasure hunt!
text_fidelity_b: WireJewelry Double Barrel Rock Tumbler with (2) 3 Pound Capacity Drums

Harry Potter Hogwarts Battle Cooperative Deck Building Card Game | Official Harry Potter Licensed Merchandise | Harry Potter Board Game | Great Gift for Harry Potter Fans | Harry Potter Movie artwork Great fun. Nice cooperative game to play with others to avoid hurt feelings, players "out of the game", and to make things feel low-stakes and casual. You never really rely on others players, it's just that some players can help each other out when possible, but no one loses before anyone else. You all lose at once.

There aren't any story events from the books during each year. As you progress through years, your character cards swap out for older portraits and new enemies and spells are introduced, but your starting character spells never change. You always have to rebuild the deck and gain low level spells even in later years, which seems pretty silly. The strategy can be dumbed down after a while and it really just depends on who the starting villains you get dealt are. You could spend as long as you want building your deck if you get someone like Crabbe and Goyle in the first round.

Dont expect this to be story-rich or something. Seems to just be harry potter themed, in the sense that this could really be almost any other story or universe that has multiple books or a serialized progression and it would also have worked fine. They just happened to pick Harry Potter. That could be a good thing however, since you essentially need zero harry potter knowledge to play.

Baby Alive Lulu Achoo Doll, 12-Inch Interactive Doctor Play Toy with Lights, Sounds, Movements and Tools, Kids 3 and Up, Brown Hair This baby alive doll was an excellent find. From the moment I pulled her out of the Amazon box, she has been my youngest new favorite thing. It's been a couple of weeks now and my daughter still carries her around the house all day long. I was worried some of the features would get "old" and then soon we just have another doll to add to the toy pile. Lucky, that hasn't happened the thrill hasn't worn off. This achoo doll is very captivating.
This doll's features are just to cute too. When her cute little button nose turns pink, even I can barely stand it... my instincts tell me to go fix it, lol. Needless to say, my daughter absolutely loves taking care of her sick baby. It's the diagnosing and healing her baby's ailments with medicine that is very rewarding. Plus, all the accessories that come with a doll are cute too.
But what I like the best about the doll is she is inspiring additional pretend play. My daughter has pulled out her doctor kit far more often and is inventing other problems to fix, lol. Over all it's a really cute doll and my daughter is getting her money's worth. I probably wouldn't recommend this for a very young toddler or as a child's first baby doll. The achoo version is little big and clunky in comparison, and doesn't feel like a traditional newborn baby doll. That's not to say that I don't recommend this one because I certainly do. It just feels like a step up from the first round of baby doll to me. But even then, I bet kids who aren't into swaddling and carrying around newborn baby dolls, would still love this because of the interactive features. And even cut my older preteen boys playing with it, so kids of any age do enjoy it!
Hope this review is helpful.

LEGO Star Wars Millennium Falcon Microfighter 75193 Building Kit (92 Pieces) If you have a 6 year old who is into Star Wars and who also loves Legos (or maybe you would like to get them into Legos and/or Star Wars), then this is a great Lego kit to do just that. I bought this and the one with the bad guy for my son's Easter Basket. Being a "connoisseur" of Star Wars and Legos, my son lost his mind when he saw what the Easter Bunny brought.

The Lego Microfighters are mini vehicles you build, which you can use to either expand your Lego-verse or play with separately. These come with instructions on how to build the microfighter. They are simple to put together, but I would not advise this for a child younger than 6 unless you know your 4 or 5 year old is really good at Lego instructions (which are in picture form). These are not ideal for children who are still primarily freebuilders or just learning about Legos. You should get the creative set for that. However, if your child loves to freebuild, but can also follow instructions this is a great gift! My son built all of the microfighters as designed, played with them for a bit, and then rearranged them to his freebuilding heart's desire. I cut the instructions apart and rearrange them in plastic sleeves so that if he wants to build according to the instructions they are neat and organized. Also do not let the "Micro" fool you, they are regular sized Legos, they will work with other Legos, it's just that they are really small scaled models. Also, the Lego people (Chewbacca) that come the sets are regular sized Lego people. So, their body parts can be mixed and matched with others you have in your collection.

One Caveat: For some odd reason, these sets as well as some of the smaller Lego City sets always have their boxes just crushed and in horrible shape. So, if you are looking for these are gift, I usually purchase from a store like Target, Walmart, or the Lego store itself to pick out the very best box. I'm not sure why Lego does this. I used to blame Target, but then I realized this was a Lego issue and not a store issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Millennium Falcon Microfighter 75193 Building Kit (92 Pieces)

Crayola Triple Tip Markers, Washable Markers, 15 Vivid Colors, 5 Count Soooo, I had high hopes for these markers. I thought my little one would be highly amused by writing in three colors at once (she was mildly amused for a short period of time). I think the issue is that in order to get the even three color lines when writing or stamping or coloring, you have to hold the marker perfectly upright and ensure all three tips are somewhat evenly on the paper. This is not easy for little hands (my little one is almost 3). I myself had to concentrate to create the images I posted. It's much easier to end up with 2 of the colors in a line or even one depending on how you hold the marker.

text_fidelity_a:
Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+ Initially I bought Snap-Circuits for my 4 and 5 year old boys. I found the collection of capacitors, resistors, integrated circuit modules, and transistors was a little too abstract, and I was thinking I really wanted more stuff like electro-magnets, relays, motors, generators, switches, potentiometers, and maybe resistive loads like light bulbs and diodes -- more basic electrical stuff, of which there's some in the circuit kits but not a lot.

My boys are 5 and 6 now. I added Snaptricity to our collection of mostly unexplored Snap-Circuits, and suddenly they're creating all kinds of basic circuits with switches, buttons, lights, motors, and electro-magnets. They're starting to understand the flow of electricity, polarity, magnetism, and resistance (as they add more loads to their circuits). I've set the transistors and stuff aside for now, because there's tons of stuff to do with these more basic components first. For older children, they might be ready for the electronic components sooner, but with my younger kids, these electrical parts are great.

We do not follow the instructions. So it helps to have extra components on hand instead of the minimum number required for the book experiments. Some of our circuits are more than elegant and minimalist. I recommend buying two kits, or this kit and another one like the 100 or 300.

The brilliant thing about these components is the incredibly simple and effective button snap-connectors. The only downside to these components is they are encased in plastic for durability. The plastic is clear so the internal components can be seen. This is really a good thing, but it's worthwhile to have a coil/electromagnet that is un-encased, as well as a speaker/microphone (electromagnet with a diaphragm) that is not encased, and a motor that can be disassembled/dissected.
text_fidelity_b: Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset There's a lot to love about sets like this that can be combined with other sets and used in creative ways. However, I'll say right up front that the whole point of getting this one is that you get the power booster, and the power booster, in my view, could use a big overhaul in the design.

Is it fun? Yes, without a doubt, the power booster is pretty fun. The problem? First of all, it takes 4 D batteries. Who uses D batteries nowadays? I'm lucky that we had just the right number of D battery adapters that allow us to use AA batteries instead, because otherwise I would have been in for a trip to the grocery store and I don't think it would've come cheap. What a power hog!

Second, the battery area needs to be taken apart with a screwdriver. This is fine for toys meant for the under three crowd, but for kids old enough to use a hot wheels set, it seems a little excessive and pretty irritating that every time a new set of batteries I need to become Mr. fix it and get out a screwdriver.

Third, when you actually go to play with it, the power booster is either on or off. So when the kid forgets about the hot wheels set and wanders off to go do something else, it's still sitting there using up your expensive D cell batteries. It's also noisy. I would've much preferred a button on the top that is easy for children to press that makes it work for a short period of time, such as 30 seconds. I'm guessing it is too much to ask to have a motion sensor turn it on or off or anything like that, so a limited time button that the child can find easily and press in the midst of gameplay without turning the power booster upside down would have been ideal.

That said, I think my primary criteria for evaluating hot wheels set is whether it is fun. Not fun for me, but fun for my kids. With only a little bit of help getting things set up, my three-year-old has been playing with this vigorously for two days and shows no signs of getting bored with it. We actually have a manual hot wheels ejecter to where you pull the lever back and press a button to make the car go really fast, and instead of using the power booster, we set that up for him to play with it on his own. The power booster is fun for when you make a big elaborate set up and are playing with a group of kids or with a parent for an extended period of time but to be honest I think when the batteries run down we may not replace them until there is a compelling reason to do so. It's just too noisy, and requires too much intervention from the parent to turn it on and off when it is needed and not just leave it noisily running and eating up our batteries.

The loop the loop works great with either the power booster or the manual ejection thing we already owned, and the tracks of course work with all of our other hot wheels sets.

I would probably recommend this most for people who have multiple children who will be playing with large and extended sets of hot wheels for 30 minutes or longer at a stretch. Otherwise, the power booster seems silly and kind of a waste.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset

text_fidelity_a: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney This game is harder than you might think. I thought my Disney knowledge was pretty good, but I was stumped on maybe 1/3 of the questions during the two games I played. My younger Disneyphiles did about the same as me. You might remember that the caterpillar in Alice in Wonderland is blue, but can you recall the color of the flags that sit atop the hats of the Tweedles? There are some questions that require you to come up with as many as five different colors, all of which must be correct for you to gain a point. What color is Celia's dress from Monsters Inc? What three colors are seen in Go Go Tomago's superhero suit from Big Hero 6?  You need to answer quickly, by putting down your selected color cards in front of you. This is actually pretty fun and interesting. Minor characters can be especially tricky. There were a few cards with answers that we disagreed with, such as the one that said Joy from Inside Out wore a yellow dress, when we all see it as green. The answer cards all have pictures from the animated films, and sometimes the photo is not great quality. My family enjoyed this game despite these issues and found it a more challenging activity than we had anticipated. It takes almost no time to learn how to set up and play. You can fill ten minutes or half an hour easily.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney

da Vinci's Room Awkward Turtle The Word Party Card Game with a Dirty Sense of Humor for Groups of 4 or More People Gave this as a gift to a recipient out of state- Due to that fact, I never felt capable of reviewing the product. Craziest thing… almost a year later, when we went On vacation and met up for dinner at the house I sent this too..(can you follow that..?!) to my happy surprise- they were all playing awkward turtles!! Yep, the game I had sent to them almost a year prior!! (could have been contrived Sure-but, from the wear and tear on the game… I knew they had been using it all along.)

Of course, we went to have Dinner with the adults at the house.. But, their group of teen/20+ yr olds were laughing hysterically in the other room having “game night“ and I promise, they were having way more fun than we were!!

I peaked in on the gameplaying and the concept looked pretty straightforward. Basically, divided into two teams… One member has an awkward word and tries to describe it to their team- if guessed correctly they get points! And the game sort of back-and-forths from there… Funny, quirky, annoying, cringe worthy, racy words all make up the options.. These kids were playing the game when we arrived- 2hr. Later we left... And they were still playing! (No! Not the same round but, plenty of rounds and all entertained long enough to still be having fun hours later.)

To me, this is the best type of endorsement one can have… Seeing a game in action and hearing the laughter as it was being played. This told me all I needed to know… The game was a hit for the crowd at hand- it kept them happily playing for hours. Combined it with the ease of which it takes to “learn” the game.. And you’ve got a winner in my book!

Parentswell Inflatable Mermaid Pool Floats, 71'' Swimming Pool Tube Mermaid Floaties, Huge Pool Float for Adults, Mermaid Swim Tubes for Pool Party Lounge Birthday Gift Having an inground pool means constantly looking for ways to enhance the experience. We don’t do much actual swimming in our pool. We mainly hang out and float, so having pool floats is a necessity. A recent addition to our backyard recreation was this inflatable Mermaid Pool Float from Parentswell.

Pulling this float from the package and unfolding it, you can see that it’s going to be larger than most, and it is. The lengthy tail is the reason. Inflating it will require a powerful set of lungs, since it is larger than average. I didn’t have a suitable pump for mine, so I did have to inflate the old- fashioned way. In fact, I would say that the cuteness factor is possibly it’s strongest point. It will be a huge hit with anyone who love mermaids.

Pools are better when you have things to enhance the experience. This float from Parentswell is a good one overall. It can take time to inflate but once ready, it holds its own and it does look cute inside my inground pool.

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Spin Turn Track Extension I grabbed one of these the same time as I purchased the Turn Kicker. Initially I thought this would somehow be similar, in that it would shoot the cars out of a curve, but this is different. Basically, your car goes up a small ramp, into an enclosed compartment which rotates 90 degrees and releases the car down a ramp on the opposite side of the track. The ramps's are not steep, so if you set up the Spin Turn at ground level, it won't travel too far when it gets released. What's cool is, you can either have it trigger another stunt, or set up the Spin Launch high off the ground (via books or trestles), so when a car gets dropped off on the opposite track, it will have lots of gravity to continue on.

The Usual Issue:
Upon assembly (which is super simple), once you attach the white roof to the Spin Turn's car base, you can't take it apart. It's already near impossible to put all pieces back in their box, but this just makes it a definite nope! Sounds like a recurring problem with many other Hot Wheel Sets... because it is.

I wonder if a better name could have been chosen than "Spin Launch"? It gives the impression that the car is getting launched like it does with many rubber band-triggered accessories. The car is only getting transported to another ramp. They should have called this the Turn Kicker, and the other accessory the Spin Launch.

Overall, I DO like the effect. Many stunts go so fast that it's over before you know it. This gives you a moment to at least watch it make the transfer. By all means, the transfer is quick, but not one of those blink of the eye or miss it stunts. A worthy add-on.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Spin Turn Track Extension

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set Ok first let me say, we are a "it's Lego or its crap" family. My kids evangelize on the evils of Megablocks and other brands they consider knock offs. But this is such a well engineered and detailed set that my fifteen year old wasn't even grudging when he said, this is a really good set.

And he's right, the detail on this set is super impressive. My son loves it for what seems like very authentic design from a war historian rather than a gamer, so maybe a fan of COD would like it even more.

This is a very challenging build, filled with small parts and unlike Lego that pre bags parts so you can open a single bag to do the first couple pages of instructions, mega blocks has you open 80% of the bags for the first few pages. You end up with an impressive pile of pieces out there. Also unlike Lego, mega blocks will create molded pieces specific to a model so realism can be pushed farther than Lego does. In this set, the body is filled with parts that are not just molded to shape but also in color to seem camouflaged or dirty from use. This truly lends a wonderful realism to the model. We also appreciated that markings are screen printed onto pieces rather than using stickers. Kudos for doing that it makes it feel like a quality set.

I do notice a bit more brittleness in the blocks and brick for brick the quality does not seem to match lego, but I can do little but rave over this set. It is beautiful, it took my son and I working together to get this done in several hours. And once done, this is a beautiful set for display.

Well done Mega Block, you are doing what I thought was impossible, you are winning us over from Lego.

*** additional

My son wanted me to mention that the instructions were hard, I would use challenging. But one thing I did forget, I am partially colorblind and often found it hard to distinguish colors in the instructions if it was not daylight.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set

Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog Sometimes when I get a box of Bloks, I chuck the instructions, dump them in with the rest of my collection, and make something cool with some of my favorite new pieces. I really liked the look of this one though, and I haven't followed the instructions for a while, so I actually built it to spec. I wasn't sure if there was any logic to all the separate and nested baggies, but half way through I concluded that the answer was "very little". I dumped them all in a dark colored jewelry display tray and things went much more smoothly. I definitely learned a few things about how some of the pieces can work together, and the end result came out looking nicer than most of the pre-built toys out there these days, but fully customizable. There are quite a lot of Bloks left over after completing the main instructions, and they've included some suggested modifications with build instructions, like the missile launcher in one of the pictures.

There were some minor flaws. The windshield doesn't attach very solidly. The two dudes are so burly and heavily armored that they don't fit inside gracefully. A few of the pieces shrunk just enough when they cooled that they ripple a bit differently than the things they are supposed to look smooth with. Lastly, while the instructions are very good, this set is mostly different shades of black and dark silver, which weren't adequately differentiated in the pictures which made locating the right parts in the heap difficult

The build process, with its sorting and instruction struck me as.something that would be a good project to do with my 3 year old son, since he is developing all the needed skills right now. Maybe instead of a puzzle, we'll build a warthog together on the next rainy day.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog

Classic Mancala Game - Features A Full-Sized, Solid Wooden Board with Exquisite Detail Stones by Pressman For 2 Players I do not play Mancala regularly but it is something I do enjoy, and I looked to this set as one I could take to the office to enjoy with coworkers. It’s a decent set up it lacks some fit and finish that would make it better.

Included in the set is the Mancala board and a plastic bag with multiple colored stones. There is also a concise rulebook on how to play one variant of the game - overall, a decent starter set.

There are several things about this set that make it less than ideal. The most serious problem is the board which has multiple issues. First, it feels unfinished with several very rough spots that are actually visibly rough. This doesn’t make the game unplayable but it does take away. My board is not routed properly and it looks like the design was routed by hand and wasn’t cleaned up properly with wood shavings wedged in the grooves. The reservoirs are shallow and it is easy to spill the stones while playing.

The stones are another matter. There are enough stones to play. However, there are no extras at all and if one or more are lost the game cannot be played correctly without replacements. And, there’s no container beyond a cheap plastic zipper bag for the stones; a cup with a snap-on lid, or a cloth pouch, would be so much better.

This is a playable and functional set, lacking in finishing touches that differentiate it from a good one.
text_fidelity_b: Classic Mancala Game - Features A Full-Sized, Solid Wooden Board with Exquisite Detail Stones by Pressman For 2 Players

Springbok Puzzles - Eiffel Magic - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle - Large 30 Inches by 24 Inches Puzzle - Made in USA - Unique Cut Interlocking Pieces At 1000 pieces, this SPRINGBOK EIFFEL MAGIC JIGSAW PUZZLE (1000 Pieces) is definitely an “expert” puzzle. However, it goes together very quickly, because it has large blocks of unique colors--if you color-sort your pieces at the beginning, the jigsaw morphs into a series of much smaller jigsaws.

My puzzle, received in March 2019, had ALL of the pieces. No surprise, because I’ve assembled many, many Springbok jigsaws in my lifetime, and have never found one to be less than perfect. (The negative reviews suggest that Springbok temporarily had a quality control problem with this puzzle design. I sympathize with the people who received defective puzzles--even though Springbok will replace a defective puzzle, any guarantee is cold comfort when you finish a jigsaw and discover pieces missing.)

Though I wasn’t crazy about the picture, I ended up loving this jigsaw, and am saving it to put together a second time. It’s really fun to assemble, because the crazy-shaped pieces let you find fits by overall shapes as well as by design colors and patterns. There are very few dark or ambiguous pieces that are hard to place in a particular area of the design.

The only thing that I didn’t like about the puzzle is that two pieces frequently slide together side-by-side to make holes for the tabs of other pieces. This means that when you assemble a small area (e.g., the pink automobile in the middle), you can’t easily pick it up to move it to the correct location. You have to slide the assembly across your tabletop, or slide a sheet of paper under the assembly to support it as it’s moved.

Note that this is a very large (30” x 24”) jigsaw. Check to make sure that it will fit on your tabletop.
text_fidelity_b: Springbok Puzzles - Eiffel Magic - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle - Large 30 Inches by 24 Inches Puzzle - Made in USA - Unique Cut Interlocking Pieces

Thames & Kosmos My City | Family – Friendly | Legacy Board Game | Kosmos Games | 2 to 4 Players | Ages 10 and Up | Award Winning Designer Reiner Knizia , Blue We have never played a legacy game like this before. I like that the rules are pretty easy and it works a little like tetris as you try to cover space and penalty areas with rocks while protecting bonus areas with trees. It is a nice little exercise in spatial relations and simple long term strategy. We actually restarted once a couple of us had epiphanies about what they should have done. But the kind of cool thing is that as you go on and build on what you know and have played, your open new rules and get new pieces introduced that again challenges your placing skills. I found it to be a unique game. We played it with four people ages 13-50s and it played well for those ages, but might not be good for the under 10 crowd. Also, the game took a few evenings, so you need to be able to put the game aside and have the same players available to pick it up again.

The game pieces are nice and I love the enveloped stages. It is a well made game and a good idea. Simple to play, but with enough mental challenge to get you thinking a little. Love it for its uniqueness and I think we will be able to play through it again a couple times.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos My City | Family – Friendly | Legacy Board Game | Kosmos Games | 2 to 4 Players | Ages 10 and Up | Award Winning Designer Reiner Knizia , Blue

Money Savvy Pig - Pink Money Savvy Pig offers a fun and effective way to teach kids about money and its many important uses. Parents devote very little time to the concept of financial management, in spite of its critical nature, often because they are not sure how best to approach the subject. Money Savvy Pig makes it easy to introduce youngsters to these important concepts.

How does Money Savvy Pig work as an educational device? The answer is simple. By including four different chambers with different labels- one for spend, one for save, one for donate, and one for invest- kids gain a sense of financial management and money allocation. They learn that money has uses that go far beyond ordinary spending. Kids under the age of seven are not ready to learn the specifics of these different concepts, but early exposure is a good idea and the Money Savvy Bank Pig certainly succeeds in this respect.

The Money Savvy Bank is made from plastic and mine has held up fine thus far. Others have pointed out that this bank can break if dropped on a hard surface. Considering its lightweight design, it isn't difficult to imagine the bank breaking apart if mishandled, which is why parents need to exercise caution and make sure their kids handle the bank with extra care when moving from one place to the next.

I like that this bank separates money into four different sections and I like that it gets kids thinking about money and its uses. One limitation, however, is that this bank isn't very good for storing paper money. The reason is because the pieces of paper are difficult to remove. The openings on the bottom of the bank are small- too small to stick your hand inside the bank to remove paper. Place a folded dollar bill inside this bank and it will take some shaking and maneuvering to remove it from the bottom. Thus, this bank should be avoided for storing paper currency. It is intended for use with coins.

Financial literacy is important and kids need to learn about money at the youngest age possible. The Money Savvy Pig is a very good piggy bank for youngsters and its benefits go far beyond the encouragement of savings. It encourages kids to ask questions and think about money in different ways, making it a great choice for a child's early financial education.
text_fidelity_b: Money Savvy Pig - Pink

LEGO Juniors Cruz Ramirez Race Simulator 10731 Building Kit If you are not familiar with the Lego Junior sets, here is the run down. The Legos are same size as the regular Legos. So tiny pieces for you to step on and feel a pain beyond your wildest imagination is highly probable. These are not a size of Lego that is between Duplo and Lego, which is what I initially thought they would be. It's what I hoped they would be. Instead, Lego Juniors are the first step to learning how to build sets with Legos using instructions. There are fewer pieces and the builds are more simplified for a younger child.

The instructions are similar to Ikea instructions, no words, but pictures that show you each step towards your newly assembled Danish minimalist furniture. The instructions are actually easy to follow and my five year old can mostly figure it out. However, I would not recommend this for any child under the age of 5, and I would highly advise to supervise while building. When I mean supervise, I don't mean just be in the room. I mean actually be there next to your child. Why? Because at 4-6 years of age, kids want to play with the Legos. It's not about building and then displaying them, they want to actually roll the cars around and move the people and have the cars crash into each other and the people jump off of buildings. Why is this a problem? It's not a problem until the pieces go missing and then you cannot build the set anymore. Lego Juniors does not realistically take into consideration that its intended age target plays rough and they are not going to be mindful to keep track of all the pieces. Thus, this exposes one of the issues with specific building sets. With free form building sets losing several pieces this is not much of an issue, but since every piece must be placed in a specific order, upon losing several, the set becomes unusable.

All that being said, if you kid loved Cars 3 and loves Legos, then this is the set for you. Just to give you an idea, this item retails for $9.99. Over the holidays, it was on sale here on Amazon and at places like Target, Walmart, and ToysRUs for $7.99. I've seen it retail for $12.99 at small business toy stores.

In addition, do not buy any Lego building set without a Lego tool. A lot of these sets have flat pieces that will get stuck and the Lego tool is your only key to sanity of getting those buggers apart! [[ASIN:B0076VIZBW LEGO Classic Brick Separator 630 Building Kit]]
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Juniors Cruz Ramirez Race Simulator 10731 Building Kit

Spin Master Games MASH, Fortune Telling Adult Party Game, for Ages 17 and up Back in the late 1980’s and early 1990’s I used to play MASH in school. No, it had NOTHING to do with the sitcom that some might remember.

The MASH game was an acronym for:

Mansion
Apartment
Shack
House

It was sort of a future/fortune telling game mainly for giggles. The original paper game was of course to tell you what “crush” you ended up with, what kind of “housing” you resided in, what you drove, and how many kids you had. One person drew a circle/swirl, like in this game, and you said STOP to get the “counter” number to begin the fortune telling – crossing off at the count.

This is an updated version of that game, though in all honesty, not near as much fun.

The basic model was to list MASH and three other variables – kids, car – crush. Like this one; you swirled and counted until you came to the end.

This game, while more grown up, is nothing like the old game even with the introduction of “scenarios”. Sadly, this is pretty much paying for something that you can get for free – sometimes you can even add more to the choices – pets, location, job(s) … with the old version, the only limitation is imagination.

This game does pay homage to its origins and includes the ORIGINAL MASH “scenario” card though the choices for everything is left up to the “decks” and not the players’ imaginations. That was, again the entire fun of it.

Depending on exactly what you’re looking for with this game – it might be best to save your money and write it out like I did or look online for MASH game cards. There are really cute printable ones out there.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Master Games MASH, Fortune Telling Adult Party Game, for Ages 17 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights GeoSafari Fossil Excavation Kit, Kids Science Kit, Dinosaur Science Toy, Ages 7+ All of the fossils were in a single spot, and it took only a second to find them. I soaked the block in water, as I didn't want to take hours to dig them out, and after a little bit, I was able to pull the fossils out of the block with ease. I got this kit specifically for the trilobite, as I have always wanted one and didn't have one yet. So imagine my dismay when my new trilobite is crumbling to pieces in front of me. It couldn't have been damaged by my not digging correctly, as I didn't even dig at all.

I looked it over and I was upset to find spots that had been glued together. That tells me they knew it was coming apart when they included it. I guess they thought it was going to go to a kid who would just assume they broke it by being careless and would just throw it out and not care, but I personally don't like that they included a piece that was crumbling. There are other reviews that have the same problem with their trilobite crumbling and there are also others with pictures of the same.

The other fossils are all fine, and if you don't care at all about the trilobite, then I guess this kit is still ok to get. But I can't bring myself to recommend it to anyone because they knowingly included a broken and glued back together fossil.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights GeoSafari Fossil Excavation Kit, Kids Science Kit, Dinosaur Science Toy, Ages 7+
